reforms.description: Japan announced measures to promote inward direct investment by removing unnecessary regulations and implementing policies to reduce start-up costs for new foreign investors, including low-interest loans and tax incentives.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The measures are designed to stimulate economic activity by attracting foreign investment, which can lead to increased productivity and innovation.
reforms.status_evidence: The measures have been put into effect to facilitate foreign investment.
reforms.importance_rationale: The reform represents a significant structural change in Japan's approach to foreign investment.
reforms.source_quote: In July 1995, Japan announced measures to promote inward direct investment by removing unnecessary regulations and by implementing policies to reduce the start-up costs for new foreign investors.

reforms.description: Japan and the United States decided to harmonise their patent systems to improve intellectual property protection, including accepting initial patent filings in English and accelerating examination processes.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Harmonising patent systems enhances intellectual property protection, which can encourage innovation and investment in new technologies.
reforms.status_evidence: The agreement to harmonise patent systems has been formalised but not yet fully implemented.
reforms.importance_rationale: This reform represents a major change in the intellectual property landscape, facilitating international collaboration and innovation.
reforms.source_quote: Japan and the United States decided, in 1994, to take measures to harmonise their respective patent systems in order to improve intellectual property right protection in the two countries.
